utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case Number IT-98-29-T, the Prosecutor versus Stanislav Galic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. Before I give the opportunity to the Defence to cross-examine Mr. Cutler, I would like to make a few observations. First of all, it might be that there will be some slight changes in the schedule for the hearings. This is not definite yet, but I thought it better to inform the parties right away so that at least they can prepare for it, that could result in the Chamber sitting on the Monday, the 3rd of June, not during the usual half day hours, but during the whole day, according to the schedule we often used in the beginning, that is from 9.30 to 1.00 and from 2.30 p.m. to 4.00. It is not sure yet, but we might change the schedule. And another possible change in the schedule might be that we would be sitting on Monday, the 17th of June, according to the same schedule, that is 9.30 to 1.00 and then 2.30 to 4.00, but then we would not sit on Tuesday. But if there would be so, sitting during the Monday a bit longer and not on Tuesday, if there is any definitive decision on that, the Chamber will immediately inform you. Then another issue we still have to decide upon is a request made by Mr. Ierace on the 23rd of May. He asked whether in respect of the report of Richard Philips, whether all the hard copies of the relevant excerpts should be provided with the report of Mr. Philips. The documents are referred in a rather long list of references, a 63-page document. The question was whether all these, the hard copies of those documents should be provided to the Chamber with the report. At this very moment, the Chamber doesn't think that it is necessary to tender all these documents. It would be an enormous pile of documents, but, of course, if the parties would refer, specifically refer, to one of these documents or rely on one of these documents, then they would have to be tendered additionally. As far as the Chamber understands, both parties have all these documents. So that is an answer to a request made by Mr. Ierace. Mr. Mundis, I take it that you will communicate this to Mr. Ierace. I think we are then at the point -- perhaps not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Just one matter of clarification, if I may, Mr. President. When you say that we would not sit on Tuesday, are you referring only to Tuesday, the 18th of June?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just that one Tuesday. So we will sit on Monday, the 17th, and not on Tuesday, the 18th. Yes, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour, the Defence only wants to inform the Trial Chamber - of course with your permission - that we would both like to interrogate the witness Cutler, in which would be more efficient, and we will only take the time that the examination-in-chief took. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Pilipovic. It seems that you already know what is on my mind now and then. Then, please, Mr. Usher -- Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. You know what I have on mine for sure. I have already managed to block my machine and I need some assistance, some technical assistance. My machine has already crashed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it crashed or is it disconnected?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, that might be a translation problem, I don't know. I can't use it any more.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: While one of the -- one of those in the technical booth can assist -- while he is assisting Mr. Piletta-Zanin, perhaps at the same time, could Mr. Usher escort Mr. Cutler into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Cutler. Please be seated. May I remind you, Mr. Cutler, that you are still bound by the solemn declaration you gave at the beginning of your testimony. Before we continue, I wonder, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, is your technical problem such that we could not continue at this moment or --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please continue, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, you will be cross-examined by counsel for the Defence and simultaneously some computer work will be done for the Defence. Ms. Pilipovic, is it you who will start?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Cutler, good day.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, in the course of examination-in-chief, you told us that you held the post of Senior Military Observer in the former Bosnia-Herzegovina, that is to say, in Sarajevo, on the 21st of December, 1992. You assumed this post on that date; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assumed the appointment -- I arrived in Sarajevo on the 21st of December, assumed the post on the 26th of December, the day that Lieutenant-Colonel Mole departed.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When you say that Mr. Mole left, could you tell us whether Mr. Mole informed you about the situation in Sarajevo? And when I say, "informed you about the situation in Sarajevo," I am referring to the positions of the warring factions in Sarajevo and the positions of the heavy artillery which was in the possession of the warring factions in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he did inform me in general terms, not the exact positions because I went on my familiarisation tour to check that for myself, under his arrangements, which I was very grateful for.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cutler. Could you confirm whether at the position that you took over from Mr. Mole, was Mr. Grier at that position before Mr. Mole, another person from New Zealand? Do you know anything about this?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not as it is spelled there, G-r-i-e-r. In fact, it is G-r-a-y. It was a Lieutenant-Colonel Gray, if that is the person you are referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cutler, thank you. Mr. Cutler, in the course of the examination-in-chief, you told us that one of your tasks as a United Nations observer, one of your tasks, according to the mandate, was to monitor and to report on the agreement that had to do with weapons concentration areas; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, were you aware of the fact that Mr. Gray, while he had his mandate up until September 1992, were you aware of the fact that he signed the weapons concentration agreement, the heavy weapons concentration agreement, in Sarajevo, of collecting the weapons, heavy weapons in Sarajevo and its surroundings, and he signed this agreement with representatives of the warring factions, to be more specific, he signed this agreement with the Muslim and the Serbian side? Are you aware of the fact that such an agreement was signed?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I was aware that there was an agreement for Sarajevo, heavy weapons concentration on both sides.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you tell us that you were aware of this, could you tell us whether you had the opportunity of having a look at this agreement, having a look at the agreement in its written form?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do recall seeing that agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, the Defence has a sufficient number of copies of this agreement that Mr. Cutler has been telling us about. We would like this agreement to be presented. It was made on the 15th of June 1992, and it was signed by Stjepan Siber, representing the Bosnia and Herzegovina side, and Mr. Radovan Karadzic signed it on behalf of the Serbian side. Could Mr. Cutler confirm whether this is the agreement in question, whether this is -- whether these are the agreements that were implemented. I have marked with 109 the copy, both the copy signed by Mr. Karadzic and the copy signed by Mr. Stjepan Siber, and there are a sufficient number of copies.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Might the interpreters be given a copy as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, do you have copies for the interpreters as well or are you not going to --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I didn't make any copies for the interpreters, but I do think there are enough copies for the interpreters, if necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: If you would like to be -- part of the document be read, then of course we have two D109s.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this is -- yes, Your Honour. Since we are dealing with two agreements at the same time, I have marked this with a number so that it is all under one number, since it is an agreement which was signed on the same day. But it was signed with Mr. Gray, Mr. Karadzic and Mr. Siber. If necessary, I will mark all those documents -- I'll mark one document with the number 109 and the other one with the number 110, but I think it is clear like this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, perhaps 109 for the -- may I call it the Siber copy and 109B for the Karadzic copy? That is Karadzic is 89 until 91 and 109 being 92 until 94. Please proceed, Ms. Pilipovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, you have two documents in front of you, or rather, two agreements dated the 15th of June. On the other side of the document, if you have a look at document 109, it's been signed by Mr. Radovan Karadzic and by Mr. Gray.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see no signatures, just indicated that where I would expect a signature, but is that --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, I just wanted to ask the witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, are the names for the Serbian side, the name of Dr. Radovan Karadzic, and on behalf of UNPROFOR, has it been signed by Mr. Gray? Can you see these two names, the name of Mr. Karadzic and of Mr. Gray in one of the documents?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see the names but no signatures. I thought the document I had seen included -- I thought General MacKenzie had actually signed the heavy weapons agreement, but I may be confusing it with the airport agreement. However, I accept the fact that those two names appear.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Cutler. And at the same time, the agreement on the airport was signed -- it was signed by Mr. MacKenzie. Mr. Cutler, the second document that you have in front of you, it says that the parties involved in this agreement, Mr. Stjepan Siber for Bosnia-Herzegovina, and on behalf of UNPROFOR, Lieutenant-Colonel Gray. Mr. Cutler, could you tell us whether within the framework of these agreements you, as a member of the United Nations who held the post of Senior Military Observer, did you implement this agreement with respect to the concentration of weapons?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I very much tried to implement the agreement, but because there was a -- what I considered to be a war going on, this was not an easy task.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, when we speak about these two documents, if I tell you that Mr. Gray in his statement which he gave to investigators for the Prosecution on the 4th and 5th of May, 1995, this document is 0090318, and I am going to paraphrase part of the statement given by Mr. Gray, according to which these agreements did not enter into force because the United Nations did not recognise Mr. Karadzic as a party who could participate in negotiations and in the signing of this agreement. This -- are you aware of this conclusion and can you accept that it is correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall that there was a lot of criticism about both the airport agreement and the heavy weapons concentration agreement. I wasn't aware of what you have just said. On Friday, I regarded the weapon -- heavy weapons concentration as being a loose agreement, and that is how I regarded it.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cutler. Mr. Cutler, if we have a look at item two in both agreements, both items start with the words: "All heavy weapons." And that is for both sides; is that correct? Is that how item two begins?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is. If we have a look at item number 4 in both agreements, the text starts with the following words: "All artilleries, mortars, tanks, armoured personnel carriers and rocket launchers, rocket systems, surface-to-surface, they shall be collected and placed under the control of UNPROFOR."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I am quite glad you gave us two copies of the agreement. One of them mentions under four armoured personnel carriers, the other one not, however. So I don't know to what -- which of the two agreements you refer. I think 109A it might be a translation problem, but not of our translators, of course. I don't know whether you have any original version available which could clarify the issue.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, thank you. The document I have was signed by Mr. Stjepan Siber. It says, "armoured personnel carriers" under item 4 for the document signed by Radovan Karadzic, so this is an original translation of those documents. It says: "rocket systems surface-to-surface and tanks." So it doesn't mention armoured personnel carriers, and that is the difference in item 4 of this agreement.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Your Honours, the interpreters apologise, but could we have a copy of the agreement, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, is this correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't find the words "rocket systems" anywhere there, I'm sorry. I've got ground to ground --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Copies will be provided to the booth.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, since we are speaking about item 4 of this agreement, which we have in front of us, could you tell us, when you took up your duties on the 26th of December within the framework of this agreement, was the role of observers which was to observe these weapons, was this role functioning?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this role was functioning and functioning quite well, but I was not convinced that all weapons were being monitored.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When you say that you weren't convinced that all the weapons were under control, are you also -- do you have both sides in mind when you say this?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have both sides in mind when I say this.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In item 6 of this agreement of the document signed by Mr. -- we can see that within the framework of this agreement signed by Mr. Siber in item 6, we can see that -- Can you hear me now?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In item 6 of this agreement signed by Mr. Siber, we can see that the Bosnian agreement agrees to up to 35 UNPROFOR personnel, and for the Serbian side, that the Serbian side agrees that up to 40 UNPROFOR personnel. Was item 6 of this agreement implemented in this manner?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 6, what I am reading, says 35 personnel, not 40. And it says: "residing at a building located next to the Presidency."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, I think the question was about both the copies of the agreement and it might be a bit misleading, but one is the agreement between the President of the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina and --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- Colonel Stjepan Siber, and the other party to the agreement, Colonel Gray. The only one, however, is the agreement on behalf of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, name of Dr. Radovan Karadzic, and signed on behalf of UNPROFOR, at least if signed, by Lieutenant-Colonel Gray. So we are talking about two different agreements, one of them mentioning 35, the other one mentioning 40. Please continue your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Yes, that is correct. The only difference is, it says, on the Bosnian side, 35 personnel residing at the building located next to the Presidency. On the Serbian agreement, it says up to 40 UNPROFOR personnel residing at Lukavica barracks. Well, in fact, when this was signed or drafted or interpreted, I am not too sure that was the intent because, in fact, the 40 personnel being correct were spread over on the Serbian side -- was spread over a number of observation posts and, of course, inside Sarajevo on the Presidency side, they were spread over a small headquarters and three observation posts within the city. So there is a difference from what is in the documents and what was actually on the ground when I took up my duties.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cutler. When you answered this question and speaking about this agreement, were you aware whether the sides that participated in negotiations, in order to sign this agreement, did these sides have any knowledge about whether the United Nations recognised this agreement or not?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not too sure I understand the question. As to the validity as of the agreement, I regarded it as a use agreement. Unless you wish to question me more on that because I am not too sure I understood the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, my question was -- had to do with the implementation of the agreement and refer to the fact of whether if you were aware during the negotiations and during contacts with both sides, both the Bosnian side and the Serbian side, whether you were aware that the parties that took part in the conclusion of this agreement, were they aware of the fact that the UN had not recognised that agreement?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that during the negotiation phase at all.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Cutler, by -- in both agreements, in item 1, a ceasefire has been noted.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that the sides respected the agreement in terms of the agreed ceasefire?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my time in Sarajevo, from the day I arrived until I left, I did not consider that there was a ceasefire in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Were you informed during your mandate until your arrival, whether the Bosnian side had undertaken certain offensive action which whereby the ceasefire agreement had been -- had been not respected?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not specifically, but I am aware that both the Bosnian and the Serb side had not respected the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, if I tell you that the Bosnian side, following June 15th, in July and August, took up the Jug offensive and then the Koverat offensive, were you aware that the Bosnian side had undertaken such offensive action?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was generally aware that there had been offensive actions within Sarajevo, but I really can't comment because I was not there at that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cutler. Mr. Cutler, when we discussed the concentration of heavy weapons, during your mandate, can you tell us which locations were under the control of the BH army and which had the greatest concentration of heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my initial days prior to Lieutenant-Colonel Mole leaving, I outlined on Friday that I visited all sites within Sarajevo. Not too distant from Papas 4, 5 and 6, there were weapons concentrations, mainly 82-millimetre mortars. I saw one tank and I saw, at the Olympic stadium, in the tunnels that would have obviously gone underneath the stadium at one stage before it was collapsed, several mortars. So to answer the question, yes, I did see the concentration of weapons within Sarajevo, and I admit to being very surprised that I did not see that many weapons.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, you answered the question about concentration of weapons which was at the Papa 4 observation points, Papa 4 and 2 -- 4, 5 and 6. Mr. Cutler, can you tell us what the concentration of weapons at Papa 1, Papa 2, and Papa 3 observation posts?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Papas 1, 2, and 3 did not exist when I took up my post. I have got a vague idea where they were, but they were not manned observation posts when I arrived in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you cannot tell us about that part of the town which was in the Papa 1, 2, and 3 observation posts and you cannot tell us about the concentration weapons of the BH army because you say such observation posts did not exist at the time?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you what I saw on my visits. Papas 1, 2, and 3 were not manned and did not exist when I arrived in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, so you cannot exclude the possibility of the existence of the BH army in that part of the town and that they had heavy weapons?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: To which part of the town are you referring, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I am referring to the eastern part of the town.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Papa 6 was in the south-eastern part of the town and I did see some weapons not too far from that location.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: As for the area of the town where the Egyptian battalion was located, subsequently, I am talking about the western part of the town, Bistrik and Velika part of the town where later on the Papa 1, 3, and 2 were stationed, can you tell us what the concentration of weapons was in that part of town?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said before, I have no knowledge of Papas 1, 2, and 3, and as for where the Egyptian battalion was in Tito barracks, there was not a weapons concentration close to that site when I was in Sarajevo, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying that there were no weapons nearby those sites, but can you tell us what were the army formations of the B and H, how were they deployed in that part of the town?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: From recollection, the ABiH army in the whole of Sarajevo was organised into about 10 brigades, and I think they may have been, when I left, trying to raise another one. As to specifically in that part of the town, are you talking about around Tito barracks or where are you talking about, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, the Egyptian Battalion had Papa 1 near the barracks -- near the part of the town called Bistrik, where there was also barracks where Papa 3 was located, the -- of the Egyptian Battalion. That was the part of the town above Colina Kapa, Velika Colina Kapa. These were hills under the control of the B and H army.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, I am aware of the area, but again I have no knowledge and cannot speak about Papas 1, 2 or 3. They did not exist when I was in Sarajevo. I was in Sarajevo from December 1992 to the 15th of March, 1993. So I do not know where Papas 1, 2 and 3 were. They did not exist under my command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, would you please proceed to another subject. We have heard five times now that the witness did not know about Papa 1, 2 or 3. So perhaps could you ask him something that he knows about?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Defence has asked this question quite consciously because we are trying to get an answer from Mr. Cutler.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: In regard to that part of the town, Mr. Cutler, you did not receive information as to what was going on in that part of town because there were no observation posts there at the time?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for clarifying that. The only thing I can recall in relation to the Egyptian Battalion Tito barracks was the fact that the Bosnians, more than once, fired mobile mortars from the location of those barracks. That is about the only information that I can give you in relation to Bosnian army activities in that vicinity.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, when you talked about weapons in the Papa 4, 5 and 2 areas, from Papa 4, that apparently there was a tank passing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, just for the sake of the transcript and the translation, the transcript says 4, 5 and 2. It is my recollection that Mr. Cutler said that he saw 4, 5, and 6, as you also repeated before. And then --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Papa 4. The position of Papa 4, you said that there was a tank in the vicinity?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Papa 4 would be -- it was on the north central side of Sarajevo, about halfway up the hill, had good observation down into the city. Down below Papa 4 some 400 or 500 metres, I was shown -- which was one of the Bosnian army concentration areas, I saw a tank. In fact, I was invited to go and see it. They were trying to get it going. It was not well maintained and they didn't think they would be able to maintain it for much longer because of spare part problems.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, can you confirm whether in the area of Papa 4 where the tank was located, in that part of the town, there was also the Kosevo stadium and the Kosevo hospital as well as the Zetra hall?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We are talking some distances between those three things but, essentially, they were in the northern part of Sarajevo. Kosevo hospital, the Olympic stadium and Papa 4 were within the same geographic area.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, were you informed that at the Kosevo stadium, the B and H army had its mortars positioned?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I told you before, I actually saw some mortars at that location.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, when we spoke about Papa 5 observation post, can you confirm that Papa 5 was near the PTT building, in that part of the town?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Papa 5 was directly due north of the PTT building by about 2.500 metres perhaps -- between 2000 and 2.500 metres. Papa 5 was on the southerly slopes of the feature known as Zuc.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, when we spoke about heavy weapons of the BH army, during your mandate, were you informed that, at Alipasino Polje, there were two tanks used by the BH army?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That location Alipasino Polje, I am not familiar with, but I understand there were a maximum of four or five tanks belonging to the Bosnian army within inside Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, if I tell you that Mr. Jackson, Brian Jackson, who as observer of the UN spent time in Sarajevo on July 24th, 1992 until January 1993, and in his statement given to the OTP on June 26th, he said that the BH army had two tanks in Alipasino Polje, would you agree with me that that piece of information or statement by Mr. Brian Jackson is correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that I knew or had been told that there were four or five tanks within Sarajevo, I could not dispute what that United Nations military observer said. I am not, however, familiar with the name of the place you just mentioned.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, if I tell you that Alipasino Polje is parallel with the Lukavica road in the area of Nedzarici and Dobrinja, near the Mojmilo hill, could this help you in orienting yourself?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, thank you. I am familiar with Mojmilo hill. I was not aware that there were any Bosnian army tanks on that hill or near that hill.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: If I tell you that Mr. Brian Jackson noted in his statement that there were two tanks in that area, can you say that this information is correct? Can you confirm that this piece of information is correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't confirm what Mr. Jackson said. All I know is that I was not aware there were any tanks at that location.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, when we spoke about heavy weapons of the BH army, during the examination-in-chief and in your statement to the Prosecution, you said that you had visited the Igman mountain. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I visited there three times, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, can you tell us whether in that part of the Igman mountain that you visited, you visited the units of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During my first visit which I had clearance for, I was only authorised to visit what was known as the "forward headquarters" of ABiH brigade that was going to be located on Igman. During that visit, and in discussions with a Lieutenant-Colonel Medo, M-e-d-o, I asked him if next time I visited, I would be allowed to visit some units in that location, and he said he would see. In subsequent visits, I asked if I could visit units and it was the preference that I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, can you confirm to us whether on February 2, 1993, from Mr. Marcetic, who was commander of the headquarters of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, that you received information as to the concentration of heavy weapons on Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Colonel Marcetic gave me that letter which was tabled on Friday. I accepted that letter from him.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, if the counsel of the Defence shows you that letter, could you refresh your recollection and confirm that the weapons that were located on Igman were weapons that you had seen when you visited the area on the basis of the letter that we have?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We would like to give the letter to Mr. Cutler, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please assist, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I just ask you, Ms. Pilipovic, before you continue, you asked the witness to confirm that the weapons that were located on Igman were weapons that you had seen when you visited the area, on the basis of the letter that we have. This suggests that, on the basis of the letter we have, we could conclude that the weapons had been seen by the witness. Of course, I had no time to study the letter in great detail but, at first sight, it indicates nothing of this kind. So would you please -- perhaps it is a matter of the formulation of the question, whether you would like to refresh the memory of the witness and ask him whether, having looked at this letter, he had seen any of the weaponry mentioned in this letter during his visits on Mount Igman, which is a totally different question from the one you put.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour, that was exactly what I had in mind when asking the question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, you have before you a letter. In the left-hand corner, it was actually addressed to Colonel Cutler; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, does it carry the date February 2, 1993 in the right-hand corner? Mr. Cutler, under number 10 [as interpreted] of that letter, you have mentioned weapons that was located in Igman and information was given to that effect by Mr. Marcetic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, this letter was handed to me by Colonel Marcetic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you are referring -- at least the translation says that under number 10. I see two series of numbers, the one going up to 9, the second one up to 7, or is there any translation problem?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I said number 9. I said from 1 to 9.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, it is in the transcript, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it is not number 10, it is number 9. That is how it says in the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, following your visit to Igman, were you able to see those weapons?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I got this letter from Colonel Marcetic, I marked the grid references on my map. Fortunately, it covered the area of Mount Igman. When I visited Mount Igman, I never saw one weapon, except individual rifles that were carried by the few soldiers that I did see. I saw, whilst driving up the winding hill up to Mount Igman, many positions that had been cut in the trees that I thought could well be used for gun or mortar positions, but I have not seen any of those guns or mortars.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, after assuming your duty and during your mandate, in addition to Mr. Marcetic who received -- who gave you this information, did you receive information from other people, from your associates, as to the effect that heavy weapons of the BH army were located on Mount Igman?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Really, the only information I had was what Colonel Marcetic had given me. Although I must add that we suspected that there were ABiH weapons on Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, did you have any information about the units which were located in Igman? Did you know whether the 4th Hrasnica Brigade was positioned in Igman?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was told that the position was a brigade position, and during my first visit, that it had not properly moved into the area. The word "4th brigade" comes to mind as possibly the brigade, but I cannot confirm that without referring to my notes. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, could you tell us or, rather, could you confirm that during the period of your mandate the so-called 7th Mujahedin [Realtime transcript read in error "Motorised"] Brigade was also in the Igman area?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot confirm that. That title of that unit, the 7th Motorised Brigade, doesn't come to mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, the Defence didn't say "Motorised Brigade," it said the "7th Mujahedin Brigade." Did you have any information about this brigade being in the Igman mountain?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry, I was reading the screen and it said the "7th Motorised Brigade." You now say the "7th Mujahedin Brigade." No, I have not heard that, however, I had heard that the brigade possibly consisted or had in it what we commonly call mercenaries. I have got no confirmation of that. I was just told that and I can't recall by who.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't hear the end of the response, "I was only told that...." Mr. Cutler, during the period of your mandate in Sarajevo, were you aware of "Operation Container"?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer to that is vaguely. I am not too sure if you are referring to the containers that were used to guard against sniping in the centre part of town or the container that kept appearing on the bridge going to the airport.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, I am not talking about the containers which had been positioned as a defence against snipers and which were used by the warring factions. I will remind you of what I am talking about. I am talking about Operation Container, the transport of weapons in lorries going to the UNHCR and escorted by UNPROFOR, and this was done in lorries taking humanitarian aid to Sarajevo. During the period of your mandate, were there any such operations of which you are aware? So under the escort of UNPROFOR members, weapons were being taken for the needs of the BH army.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The only incident I am aware of is some -- and I was aware at the time -- I think it was reported by my DSMO, Major Carswell. It was to do with gas bottles that were full of explosives. I understand that was investigated by the United Nations civilian police. I do not know too much detail about that. I am sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, I am just -- I thought we were already at the time for the break but we are not. I apologise for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, in the course of the examination-in-chief, you spoke to us about -- you said that in January, the Vice-President of the BH government was killed.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Do you know whether an investigation was initiated by members of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, given that according to the initial information this was done by a member of the Sarajevo Romanija Corps?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I recall just after that incident occurred, the assassination occurred, I think it was the next morning at the 8.30 hours conference that the force commander said it was being investigated by both the United Nations Civilian Police and that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps was also conducting their investigation.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, when you spoke to us in the course of the examination-in-chief about the protests you had addressed to Mr. Marcetic, and we are not speaking about the letters that you sent -- we are not speaking about the letters that you sent Mr. Stanislav Galic with regard to the shelling of the observation posts in regard to the shelling of Papas. We are speaking about the shelling that you mentioned, the shelling of civilian targets. Could you tell us whether these protests were oral or written?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was one written letter, from my recollection, in relation to the firing on the Kosevo hospital. Others were verbal.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So you are saying that the written document which was sent as a protest to the Sarajevo Romanija Corps, the document which has to do with the shelling of the Kosevo hospital, you are saying that all the other protests were verbal protests?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I sent many letters but the only ones I recall were to General Galic in relation to the shelling of Papa 5, a letter in relation to Kosevo hospital. There were possibly others, but my main protests in relation to sniping, shelling, firing on utilities missions, that I raised with Colonel Marcetic, were verbal, oral.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: You said that Mr. Marcetic, when you spoke to him, he said that he told you that, "It was war." In your opinion, are such answers by an officer who holds an important position, are such answers acceptable answers?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't believe they are acceptable answers, not when it involved the killing or shelling into Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, on the basis of what you can remember, can you tell us about one of the incidents with regard to which you sent a written report to Mr. Marcetic and which related to the time when you were there as a Senior Military Observer? So the time, the place and the consequence of these results, did you mention this in written form?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: It would have been after the 11th of January would have been the letter on Kosevo hospital. No, I am sorry, it would have been after the 29th and 30th of January when the Kosevo hospital was shelled. And a 155 millimetre shell as I described on Friday went into the hospital. As I understand it, the only place that shell could have come from was from the Serbian side.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, in the course of your examination, you said that you did have information about the fact that the BH army had been using mobile mortars which had been positioned next to the Kosevo hospital and that they fired shells from these mortars?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: When we are speaking about such mortars which were positioned next to the hospital, in your opinion, were such mortars legitimate military targets? So were they legitimate military targets on the side of the 1st Corps of the BH army?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The fact that there was a hospital in the area, no, I don't believe they were legitimate targets because the shells, given the natural tendency of shells to be off-line and bearing and in range, there was a very high likelihood of hitting the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, I don't think you have answered my question as to whether the mortars were legitimate military targets.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would consider mortars on the front line, not in civilian areas, to be legitimate targets, but not those located near a hospital.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: May I ask you one additional question at this very moment, Mr. Cutler? Would you consider it to be legitimate to put a mortar on hospital ground?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Under no circumstances, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So Ms. Pilipovic, what you are actually doing is dragging Mr. Cutler into a rather complex legal debate on whether illegitimate acts would justify answers. I think that, with due respect for Mr. Cutler, that this would be not a wise thing to do. That is the reason why I asked this specific question. Please proceed. Apart from that, Mr. Cutler did answer the question. He said as a matter of fact: "I don't believe they were legitimate targets." And then he gave the reason.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, when you spoke about the shelling of the airport in February 1993, could you tell us whether you determined who shelled the airport in February 1993 while you were holding your post or, rather, could you first tell us whether you know that the airport was shelled?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I covered this in some detail on Friday. I am aware of mortar rounds landing near a French observation post as you enter the airport. If I understand correctly, there was one French soldier who was killed and one was wounded in that incident. Expert crater analysis people were brought in by the sector, sector commander, and the crater analysis revealed that those rounds probably came from a Bosnian mortar.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Cutler, you are telling us that the airport was shelled by the BH army forces. Could you tell us from which locations the members of the BH army shelled the airport?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am saying only in that particular instance was it concluded that the rounds probably came from an ABiH mortar position. I personally did not see the report. It was done for the sector commander and I have no knowledge where those mortars may have fired from.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: So, Mr. Cutler, you are telling us that in the airport area, you weren't informed about where the BH army positions were?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not saying that at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Ms. Pilipovic, you are misrepresenting the testimony of the witness now several times. Would you please be more precise.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, with regard to the airport area, could you tell us -- could you tell us where the BH army positions were in the area of the airport?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, for a start, the airport as such, the runway, the buildings that were used by the French battalion and by the movement control people of UNPROFOR, there was no ABiH within the confines of that. The front lines were basically on the road to the airport which went parallel to the suburbs of Butmir, Nedzarici; and on the other side of the airport -- wrong. Run parallel to Nedzarici and Dobrinja. And then on the north-western side of the airport, ABiH in Butmir, and that would be where the ABiH front lines would have been located.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, if I tell you that in the vicinity -- that Hrasnica was also in the vicinity of Butmir but that it also under the control of the BH army, would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would, but it wasn't very close to the airport. It was under the shadow of Mount Igman.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, during the period of your mandate, were you told why there was no observation posts in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, just one more question and then I will have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was just wondering whether you were touching upon a new subject, but please finish this question.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Cutler, could you tell us whether there was an observation post in Nedzarici?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand that Colonel Gray established a -- an OP in Nedzarici. It was not there when I got there because it was too unsafe where between Nedzarici and Dobrinja, and Nedzarici and the suburb to the north, the front lines were very close, almost straight apart. I understand that Colonel Gray did establish one there early on, but there was not one there when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cutler.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I think this would be a good time to have a break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, we will adjourn until 20 minutes past 4.00 and may I indicate, Ms. Pilipovic, there is a little bit less than 50 minutes remaining time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we resume, I take the opportunity to correct myself, and that is one of the advantages of the one-half hour delay in broadcasting. Where I said that it was wise to drag Mr. Cutler in a legal debate, of course, I did intend to say that it was not wise to do so. Is the Defence ready to resume the cross-examination? Mr. Piletta-Zanin? Or is it Ms. Pilipovic?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. At your service. Mr. President, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I will allow myself to question you in French, I would like to greet you, first of all. Good day.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good day.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. And how are you?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am fine, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. Sir, in order to respect the time that we have remaining, in order to respect the time which governs all of us, I am going to ask you to reply to us as briefly as possible and, if possible, to answer "yes" or "no" when answering my questions, when answer questions which can be answered by "yes" or "no." Sir, is it true that your training as a military person involved academic training?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, to a certain degree, academic training.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, as a superior officer, you were necessarily -- you followed training which -- in international humanitarian law?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at a university level, but certainly, that was part of our training.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, would it be correct to say that members of the military are people who are precise, meticulous, and who in general express themselves briefly?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, generally speaking.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. And as a result, would it be correct to say that in your statement there is quite a lot of textual precision?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you interpret that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, thank you. I want to return to a subject. I think that you stated that in your written statement given to the Office of the Prosecutor, in that statement, you said that in one of the missions of the UN personnel in Sarajevo, it was also necessary to report on anything that was not quite usual; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, could one depart from the principle -- could one base oneself on the principle that there was a rule, the objective of which was to ensure that any officer who discovered anything that was not normal should report this event and declare that it had taken place?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I shall now turn to your -- the statement you made on Friday, and I am referring to the willingness of the British sergeant to report to you on a declaration which has to do with mortar shells being fired. Can you remember speaking about this?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember it well.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can we base ourselves on the principle that such a reaction, this type of reaction, that is to say the need of immediately informing one's superiors that something abnormal has happened, was this principle something that was the rule?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. Witness, now I would like to follow a new line of questioning. If I tell you that we have in our proceedings witnesses, at least one witness, and now from the UN family and even from the military observer UN family, stating the following: That it was common practice amongst the military observers first that the Muslims shelled each other during funeral processions. Second --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There may be some misunderstanding. I see in the transcript that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Themselves. Themselves. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, that it was common practice among the military observers; it is not what you said in French. Could you please repeat what you said in French so we can have it properly translated, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It was notorious, a notorious fact, that the Muslims shelled each other, if you like, in the following points: During funerals; two, during when they would group together to collect water; when they would assemble to buy bread; four, at marketplaces; and five, when the press was in the area, and this was the case of Markale. What would you say to that statement?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, I would say the statement is not correct except for one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would you tell --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, it is my recollection that the witness testified that it was about markets, but not Markale specifically asked for it. So -- I don't remember the bread as well but I might be mistaken. Would you be very precise --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I was very precise in French. I said it very clearly. I gave thought to the question. When the people of the press were around, as was the case in the Markale situation. We know that the press was present within the framework of Markale. I did not say that the witness had said that the Muslims had fired in the Markale case. My phrase was very clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, but just before that, you referred to marketplaces and that, of course, is almost asking for confusion, specifically because the witness said that as far as marketplaces was concerned, there was not Markale. So it is rather confusing the way you are doing it. But please proceed. I think the question is clear at least by now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, in other words, would you consider these words to have been credible or not so credible?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I have the choice between those two statements, it would have to be not so credible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: You are saying that the witness that had said that was not a credible witness, is that so?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not saying that. I -- any Muslim-on-Muslim fire would have to be proven. Whilst there were many rumours, as I said on Friday, I know of only a few instances where it was almost proved to me that that was the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Could you quote the case, please?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes. The incidents that I quoted that I recall that it was very strongly suspected that the Bosnian army fired outside the Presidency, or 100 metres to the west of the Presidency, during the visits of Vance and Owen and Boutros Boutros-Ghali.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for your answer. Do you know in your capacity of officer whether the Muslim forces had mobile equipment capable of transporting mortars?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I never saw any myself, but I understand there were several vehicles that were termed to be "mobile mortars." They were on the back of a trailer or the back of a car or some vehicle. I described on Friday the firing of one of those mobile mortars from outside the PTT and I described earlier today the firing of one of those from outside Tito barracks, where the Egyptians were based.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, thank you for your answer. Now, could you answer "yes" or "no" to the following question: Do you know where the 102nd unit of Alipasino Polje was stationed? Let's be very accurate. I said the observation post, not units. CC, common control post. Can you answer "yes" or "no"? Do you know where the CC was in Alipasino Polje, the 112th brigade?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By "CC," are you saying command post?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [In English] Command control, yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would hope that -- please be very precise. Do you know where the command post of the MUP was, Colonel, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know where the Zitsa was?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you are referring to the Olympic stadium.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I didn't mention "Zetra," I mentioned "Zitsa."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is what is in the transcript, Zitsa, as a matter of fact. Mr. Piletta-Zanin, I also noticed that in French you are speaking very quickly. So if you ask the interpreters to translate very precise, I think adjustment of your speed would certainly assist them. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, Zitsa, to be very precise, do you know where Zitsa is?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have to say no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So you don't know what was located there either?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you were to tell me what was possibly there, I might recall that, but I don't have any knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. The same question with regard to Magros?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: The word has not come up on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: M-a-g-r-o-s, Magros.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard the word but, no, I cannot tell you where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Can you tell me the same with regard to Valter Peric? Can you answer yes or no, Witness, please?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen a word like that that's in front of me on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: From the screen, you do not see the word as pronounced by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. He said, "Peric" and he spelled it P-e-r-i-c.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. Same question, please, for Stela. Same question, please, for Stela.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Other than the fact that it is a brand of beer, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Same question for Petar Derik -- Dakic, sorry. Dakic.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have seen that -- I have seen that name, but I can't tell you exactly where it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Okay. Same question for Pale Goranin.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that name is familiar to me. The exact location, without a map, I can't say.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Same question for Kulin Ban. Kulin Ban?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Same question for Gras, G-r-a-s?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have seen that on a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So where is it?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would suggest it is to the north-west of Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What was there? Please can you tell us what was there?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have a suspicion that one of the Lima positions was there, but without a map, I couldn't tell you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Are you sure that it was Lima?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, technically, is it true that it is rather -- very difficult to hear the fire of a mortar, rather than -- compared to a gunshot -- artillery shot, sorry?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily. It depends on the topography and the distance from the gun line or the mortar, mortar line.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Exactly. It is possible, Witness, that some mortar shells could have passed imperceptibly starting from the interior of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean that they were fired out without being perceived?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: It is a probability which is a certitude?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not a certainty, but it is certainly highly possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. So consequently it is perfectly probable that shooting from counter-batteries was triggered from Lima following firing from Sarajevo that had not been detected; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer, Colonel. You indicated that you know that there were mobile -- military objectives and that you said that you did not know what was in the list of names that I have just given you. -- If I tell you that the list of names corresponds in all probability to a small number of military objectives, how can you assert or confirm the existence of random firing if you do not even know where some military targets are or what is found there?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand the question. As the Senior Military Observer, I sat in the PTT. The list of names you have given me ring bells to me, but I will be not familiar with them as the UNMOs on the ground would be. In the daily reporting, they would normally give a name and a grid square, and they may have well been reported. I would have to check my sit-reps which were written every day, and I assume some of those names would crop up.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Now, let us concentrate on mobile targets. Could you totally exclude and in all honesty that when a shell was fired to the centre of the town, it was not in response by a movement of a military target, that is, a silent shot?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: By "silent shot," are you saying that there may have been movement and thus --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Let us forget that. A shot that was not detected.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could have well been the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Consequently, it is quite possible, sir, that when you define something as being a random shot, it could be a response to a provocation or to shelling; is that true?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you for your answer. So I would like to go back to a question which is -- which I am interested in. It has to do with Captain Henry [as interpreted]. You introduced him as being a young captain; is that true?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was younger than I, and anybody younger than I was young. He was about 34 at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: So younger than you which, in other words, means young. Thank you. All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we need some time to reflect on that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need time to think about the translation as usual.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, it is not quite what I said, but it isn't very important. Would it be true to say, Witness, that this young officer at the time was courageous?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think many of the UNMOs were courageous. I wouldn't put him any higher or lower than others.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I believe it is a translation error, on page 38, line 21, we're all, I think, of the same view that it should say "Captain Henneberry" rather than "Captain Henry."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that would be correct and there is no misunderstanding about it. Please proceed, Mr. Piletta-Zanin. As well, Mr. Mundis, a yellow paper would perfectly work.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, now I will get back to the question of Captain Henneberry. Could you answer "yes" or "no" to the question if this officer was an idealist or he showed a certain amount of idealism?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Would it be your impression, sir, that the officer was necessarily more impressionable given the fact that he lacked experience, comparatively, than an officer with experience like you?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you spoke to us about just a while ago about, as a general rule, that it was the obligation for military observers to report about all sorts of unusual incidents and facts; is that true?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, you were in Sarajevo at the theatre of operations in January, end of 1992, beginning of 1993; is that true?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: December 1992 to March 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What day of December was the 26th?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be guessing. It would be a -- Christmas day fell on a Sunday. A Monday or a Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Good. Perfect. Sir, is it true, as far as you know, that the end of 1992 and then in the course of 1993, one talked in the military and diplomatic circles about the creation of this Tribunal to intervene?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard anything about the Tribunal being created. What I did hear about is a list. Somebody had produced a list of war criminals which had on it Serbs and Croatians, to my knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: When did you hear that, sir?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: That would have been during my period in Sarajevo, and it was really brought to my attention when I went for a visit to Igman and passed through Hrasnica, where I kept being told it is about time that a list was produced, and that somebody had produced one, and could I get a copy of it. Which I couldn't, incidentally.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: All right. Sir, if I understand you correctly, one talked during your stay about war criminals in Sarajevo, is that true, or around Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is generally true.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Colonel, if you received any sort of information on a war criminal at that time, what would you have done?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it depends on what that information would be, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: An information, the contents of which were certain, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, would you please come to your point?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I am trying to do so, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think you understood what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: If you had received information from your services with regard to a war criminal, what would you have done in such a case?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that very much depends on what the information would be. Like, I mean, just because I may have received information -- I am not understanding what you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Very well. I am going to put this question very directly. If, sir, you had received a piece of information from one of your men, according to which -- saying that, "I had been informed of the existence of a plan in order to level with the ground the town of Sarajevo, to shell the town," how would you have reacted to this?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't have reacted much at all because, in fact, my experience since I had been in Sarajevo was, there was nothing new in that. Shelling was going on day and night.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: I will interrupt you, sir. You said that it wasn't new. I am talking about a precise piece of information on a plan coming from an army corps. And you said that that was not new, you had received other statements?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had concluded, as I said on Friday, very early on that the pattern of shelling of Sarajevo on -- the two distinct patterns are front line and shelling into the city was a fait accompli, that that's the way it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Sir, I am asking you a very precise question and I would like you to answer it very directly. Did you receive any sort of statement from anyone according to which it was affirmed in a very clear and precise way that a plan existed at the level of an army corps and this plan was to level with the ground the town or to shell mercilessly the town? Did you receive any information to this effect, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer "yes" or "no" to that. I now know what you're referring to. But to level Sarajevo to the ground, as I have not heard of any information of that nature, Captain Henneberry told me that the UNPROFOR LO at the Lukavica headquarters told him that it was intentional to shell into Sarajevo. If that is the one you are referring to, that is what he said.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, I would like to continue with this subject. I read your statement very carefully, the statement you made on Friday, and the terms you used. You used the term "interpreted," I "interpreted" this or that. Is it correct that this idea of a plan, you interpreted this, but it wasn't formulated as such?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I couldn't say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. As a result, if I understand you correctly, is it exact to say that when the young Captain Henneberry came to see you, he never directly formulated a plan?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, sorry, I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: This is the logical follow-up to your question. Is it correct, Witness, that the young Captain Henneberry, when he spoke to you, he never formally mentioned in these words, "the existence of a plan at the level of an army corps." Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not at the level of an Army Corps. Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Witness, I would like to return to Mr. Henneberry, to the Witness Henneberry. Do you know whether there are documents in which Captain Henneberry himself is asking himself whether he has been hallucinating, whether he has been a victim of hallucinations?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I am not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Do you know whether Captain Henneberry complained to you about the fact that he could hallucinate?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During the time in Sarajevo, are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: During that time or afterwards, if you met him afterwards.

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: I understand he may have had a few troubles, as did quite a few others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: What do you mean by "a few troubles"?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: Quite a few of the UNMOs that I am aware of were offered, and sought, and were given, psychological treatment after they came out of Sarajevo and I am aware that Colonel Gray, for example, sought help in that direction. I think there were others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you think that this was also the case with Captain Henneberry?

utterances.speaker: JAMES PHILIPE CUTLER [Resumed]
utterances.text: During his time in Sarajevo, I considered him to be a very professional, hard-working officer. He was obviously under a lot of stress, but I did not regard that he was anything other than fully in charge of his faculties.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the transcript, the document mentioning the fact that this person was asking himself about his hallucinations, it is P646, document P646, page 17 to 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to continue with what you stated. You stated that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
